headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can expose shared files and Opik’s broad egress can amplify leakage, while prompt-injection and cascading-error paths are otherwise limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-first and has no clipboard/MCP surfaces, so direct injection paths into Opik are not documented. However, both profiles expose API-style interfaces and ComfyUI can handle workflow/file content, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could still carry malicious instructions. The pairwise pathway is weak and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or workflow content into Opik prompts or evaluation inputs
IF a shared file or message channel is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid copying generated text between tools without review
Strip instructions from any shared artifacts
Use a fixed prompt template for Opik inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches model files and workflow assets, while Opik has broad network egress and a REST API surface. If shared data includes sensitive prompts, seeds, or model artifacts, Opik can transmit them off-host. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use once artifacts are passed between them, though the profiles do not prove an automatic shared workspace.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs or stores sensitive prompts, seeds, or workflow files that are then sent to Opik
IF Opik is configured to log or forward those inputs to its backend or API
mitigations: Do not route sensitive prompts through Opik
Redact seeds and workflow metadata before upload
Store ComfyUI assets in a separate directory
Review Opik logging settings before use
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot contend for mutable local resources with Opik from the profile alone. Opik is not runnable and exposes only a REST API, so there is no documented shared write target or locking conflict. The overlap is mostly read/observe, making conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or repository
IF a wrapper adds mutable shared state not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate directories
Avoid shared git repositories
Use read-only mounts for both agents
Serialize any external orchestration steps
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Opik is an evaluation/observability tool, so it may consume ComfyUI outputs as inputs for scoring or logging. If those outputs are treated as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated metadata from ComfyUI can cascade into Opik reports or downstream decisions. The profiles do not show automatic action-taking, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Opik ingests ComfyUI outputs as ground truth without a validation step
IF downstream automation uses Opik reports to trigger actions
mitigations: Add a human review step before Opik records conclusions
Validate ComfyUI outputs against source artifacts
Mark generated metadata as untrusted
Limit Opik to observation-only mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for transferred outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated-data commitments, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch. The only compliance concern is if an operator routes sensitive media or prompts through Opik’s broad egress, but that is not evidenced as default. The other agent is not cited separately because no distinct compliance obligation is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF Opik is used to export logs containing sensitive prompts or media
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Review retention settings in Opik
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: implement policy-based redaction before export
